issues.description: Predicate is correct but reads obliquely; a literate comment would carry it.
issues.detail: The new clause `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` encodes the CSS rule that a statement-form `@layer foo;` (no block) is permitted before `@import`, while a block-form `@layer foo {}` is not. The invariant is non-obvious to a future reader; one line of comment citing the CSS Cascade spec would make this readable without running it. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

PostCSS distinguishes container from leaf at-rules by the presence of a `nodes` array. Writing `node.nodes === undefined` (or better, `!('nodes' in node)` or a helper `isContainerAtRule`) states the intent more crisply than a `typeof` guard and matches idiom elsewhere in the codebase. Minor readability, not correctness.

issues.description: Test coverage misses the statement-form `@layer foo;` accept case alongside the new reject case.
issues.detail: The added test covers `@layer foo {}` (block, must reject). The complementary invariant — that `@layer foo;` and `@layer foo, bar;` before `@import` remain accepted — should have a paired positive test in the `accept` block if not already present, so the bisection between block and statement form is pinned by tests, not only by the implementation.

review.summary: The fix is small, local, and correct: it refines the layer-exception to apply only to statement-form `@layer` (no `nodes`), so block-form layers are treated as blocking content and trigger the rule. Complexity is unchanged (single linear walk over preceding siblings). The algorithmic invariant — "an @import is invalid if any preceding sibling is a non-import, non-charset at-rule, a non-statement-layer, or a normal rule" — is now correctly stated by the code, but it is not stated *for the reader*. Decision: RIGOROUS on logic, NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on presentation. Recommend a one-line comment and a paired accept-case test; otherwise ship.
